title: Gifts From the Sage
captions: The next morning, Vishvamitra smiled at Rama. “I am very pleased with you, my child. Today I will give you a great gift.”
Facing the rising sun in the east, the sage chanted sacred mantras. He gave Rama the divine astras, the shining weapons of the gods.
One by one, the astras appeared before Rama in glowing forms. With folded hands they said, “We are here to serve you, Rama.”
Rama touched them gently and said, “Stay in my mind, and come to me whenever I call you.”
Then Rama asked for one more thing. “Please teach me how to call the astras back, too.” Pleased, the sage taught him that as well.
Rama's heart was full of thanks. He bowed before his great teacher with folded hands.
As they walked on, Rama saw a peaceful grove at the foot of a hill. “Great sage, whose hermitage is that?” he asked.
story: The next morning, Vishvamitra smiled at Rama. He was very pleased with how the young prince had freed the land from Tataka. “Today I will give you a great gift,” he said.
Facing the rising sun in the east, the sage chanted sacred mantras. Then he gave Rama the divine astras, the shining weapons of the gods. Each astra was a power that could be called with a mantra.

One by one, the astras appeared before Rama in glowing forms. With folded hands they said, “We are here to serve you, Rama.” Rama touched them gently and said, “Stay in my mind, and come to me whenever I call you.”

Then Rama asked for one more thing. He wanted to learn how to call the astras back after they were sent out. Great power is only safe when it can be controlled. The sage was pleased with this wise request and taught him that too.

Rama's heart was full of thanks, and he bowed before his teacher with folded hands. Then they walked on, and Rama noticed a peaceful grove at the foot of a hill. He asked whose hermitage it was. The answer would lead to a new adventure.
lesson: Vishvamitra gave Rama the most precious gifts he had: knowledge and the divine astras. Rama did not grow proud. He bowed to his teacher with a thankful heart, and he even asked to learn how to call the astras back, so that such power would be used with care. In our tradition, the guru is honoured like a parent, and Kritajnata means remembering and thanking those who help us grow.
lesson_long: Kritajnata means gratitude: remembering the good that others have done for us, and thanking them.

Vishvamitra gave Rama the most precious gifts he had. Rama did not grow proud, and he did not simply take the gifts and move on. He bowed to his teacher with a thankful heart. He even asked how to call the astras back, so that such power would always be used with care.
Our elders teach that a grateful heart keeps us humble. When we remember who helped us, we are more ready to help others in turn.
tradition: In our tradition the guru is honoured like a parent, and even like God. A well known prayer says Guru Brahma, Guru Vishnu, Guru Devo Maheshwara. It means the guru is like Brahma who creates, Vishnu who protects and Shiva who removes what is not needed.
At the end of their studies, students offered gurudakshina, a gift of thanks to their teacher. It did not have to be money. The best gurudakshina is to use what we have learned well.
words: a divine weapon called with a mantra
the peaceful home of a sage, also called an ashram
a gift of thanks to a teacher
a greeting with folded hands, meaning I bow to you
question: Who is a teacher who has helped you learn something special? How could you thank them?
questions: Who is a teacher who has helped you learn something special? How could you thank them?
Why do you think Rama asked how to call the astras back?
What is something kind that someone did for you this week?
card_lesson: Rama received wonderful gifts, but he did not grow proud. He bowed to his teacher with a thankful heart. Kritajnata means remembering and thanking those who help us grow.
